title: Water Bottles
summary: Given the initial number of full water bottles and the number of empty bottles required to exchange for one full bottle, determine the maximum number of water bottles that can be drunk.
statement: Given the initial number of full water bottles and the number of empty bottles required to exchange for one full bottle, determine the maximum number of water bottles that can be drunk.
constraints: Drink every full bottle; num_exchange empty bottles can be exchanged for one full bottle.
Return the maximum number of bottles that can be drunk.
hints: Drink all currently full bottles and add them to the empty count.
Exchange as many empties as possible, retaining the remainder.
Repeat until no full bottles remain.
Each iteration performs every available exchange without losing empties, so no additional bottle can be obtained afterward.
editorial: Each iteration performs every available exchange without losing empties, so no additional bottle can be obtained afterward.

tests.explanation: Nine bottles produce nine empties, then three bottles, then one, for thirteen total.
Exchanges produce three bottles, then one more using accumulated empties, for nineteen total.
